title: Coordinate geometry
examples: How do I find the midpoint between two points?
What is the gradient if the line goes through (2, 5) and (6, 13)?
If a line is perpendicular to y = 2x + 1, what is its gradient?

explain.say: Today we learn about coordinate geometry. We use points on a graph to find things.
First we find the midpoint. To find it, you average the x coordinates and average the y coordinates.
Let us find the midpoint between point one, which is two, three. And point two, which is six, seven.
The midpoint will be at x equals four, and y equals five. So the point is four, five.
Next we find the distance. The distance formula uses the square root of the differences in x and y squared.

items: Find differences in x and y

faq.q: How do I calculate the distance between two points?
faq.a: You use the distance formula. You square the difference in the x values, square the difference in the y values, add them, and then take the square root.
asks: How do I find the length between two coordinates?

faq.q: What is the gradient, and why is it important?
faq.a: The gradient is the steepness of a line. You find it by changing in y divided by changing in x. It tells you how much the line rises for every unit it runs.
asks: How do I calculate the slope?
What does gradient mean on a graph?

faq.q: What is the midpoint formula, and can I mix up the coordinates?
faq.a: The midpoint is simply the average of the corresponding coordinates. You average the x's together and average the y's together separately.
asks: How do I find the middle point?
Is it just averaging the numbers?

faq.q: What is the gradient of a perpendicular line?
faq.a: The gradient of a perpendicular line is the negative reciprocal. If the first gradient is 'm', the perpendicular gradient is negative one divided by 'm'.
asks: If a line has gradient 2, what is the perpendicular gradient?
How do I find the slope of a line at right angles?

faq.q: How do I check if two lines are parallel?
faq.a: Two lines are parallel if and only if they have the exact same gradient. If the gradients match, the lines will never cross.
asks: What must the gradients be for parallel lines?
Are the gradients the same for parallel lines?

facts: The gradient is calculated as the change in y divided by the change in x.
The midpoint formula requires averaging the x coordinates and the y coordinates separately.
Parallel lines always have equal gradients.
Perpendicular lines have gradients that are negative reciprocals of each other.

quiz.say: Find the midpoint of the points (1, 5) and (7, 11).
quiz.why: You average the x coordinates: one plus seven divided by two equals four. You average the y coordinates: five plus eleven divided by two equals eight. The midpoint is four, eight.

wrong.1: This option adds the coordinates together instead of finding the average.
wrong.2: This option finds the sum of the x values and the sum of the y values, forgetting to divide by two.
wrong.3: This option correctly finds the average of the y values but incorrectly averages the x values by subtracting instead of adding.

quiz.say: What is the gradient of a line passing through (0, 2) and (4, 10)?
quiz.why: The change in y is ten minus two, which is eight. The change in x is four minus zero, which is four. Eight divided by four equals two.

wrong.0: This option calculates the change in y divided by the change in x but fails to simplify the resulting fraction.
wrong.2: This option incorrectly multiplies the change in y by the change in x.
wrong.3: This option incorrectly divides the change in x by the change in y.

quiz.say: If a line has a gradient of negative one half, what is the gradient of a line perpendicular to it?
quiz.why: The negative reciprocal of negative one half is two. You flip the fraction and change the sign.

wrong.0: This option correctly flips the fraction but forgets to change the sign.
wrong.1: This option only flips the fraction without changing the sign, which is incorrect for perpendicular lines.
wrong.2: This option incorrectly calculates the reciprocal without considering the negative sign.
